chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: The Echols band: first arrangements, Echols throwing his horn
summary: Echols's band was his first to play arrangements; Echols could not read and threw his trumpet in the air, and they played Solomon's dance hall.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well when you, when you get through with Charlie Echols band, were you playing arrangements with Ellighe?
Ellighe?
Yes. Oh, not with Ellighe
Not with sort of dead or...

Yes, that was just a jam session. You know like, we all play. But with Echols it was the first band that I played with that played arrangements. Except for Mouse and his Music, we used to play stock arrangements with Mouse and his Music, 'Sonny Boy' and things like that.
Mouse and his Music that was only what, six pieces?
Yes. We played stock orchestrations. Mouse and his Music.
Well who was in the Charlie Echols band?

Well that you would know, I don't think, they were all local boys and I doubt if whether any of them ever left California. I don't think any of them ever left. They were all local. It was a pretty good band. It was a good hard swinging band.

Echols was a trumpet player that never knew one note from another, but he would just act like he was playing and whatever came out of this horn it didn't disagree too much with the band but he wasn't playing anything really.
Well you mean he couldn't read?

No, he couldn't read. He didn't know one note from the other but was a nice looking guy and one of his tricks was to throw the trumpet up and in the air and then he'd catch it. And everyone thought that was great. But he broke up a lot of horns doing that. He wasn't a musician at all
Well that's what Lunceford's band used to do years ago.
That's right, throw the horn. Freddie Jenkins used to do it too. Echols would throw his higher than anybody and he used to wear those Russian, you've seen the Russian silk pyjamas?
Yes.
He'd to wear the Russian silk pajama tops....
Tight around the neck?
Tight around the neck, a belt and the rest of his pants and shoes were (ordinary?). They were nothing but sleeping pajamas, but he liked them and he wore a little white cap. (LAUGHTER).
What did the musicians in the band wear?

Well we had little Eton jackets. We had Eton jackets. We had a lot of fun. We worked at a place called 'Solomon's' dance hall. It was on Grande Street out there. A big dance hall. Where all the sailors used to go. And we did a good job. Paul Whiteman played there one time.
Oh, at the same place then?
At one time he had played way before us. It was a nice place.
Well how long were you with Charlie Echols?
